scope: Pure header/item selection for the public print_summary owner; exact original writeln!/PathBuf::display calls remain the host I/O bridge.
encoding: All fields are little-endian u64; buffers may be unaligned, must be live and disjoint.

phases.0: Initial request: group and index must both be zero; counts are arbitrary u64. Select the success header even when all counts are zero.
phases.1: Continue: group0/1/2 selects added/modified/deleted and index must not exceed its count; group3 requires index0 and selects completion.

effects.2: Write added[path_index] using the exact original A formatting call.
effects.3: Write modified[path_index] using the exact original M formatting call.
effects.4: Write deleted[path_index] using the exact original D formatting call.

selection: Advance past each exhausted group in added, modified, deleted order.
Select the first nonexhausted group at the supplied index and increment that index by exactly one.
Never aggregate the three counts; values whose mathematical total exceeds u64 remain valid.
The increment is checked after index<count, so even count=U64_MAX is safe.
At most three exhausted groups are visited per invocation.
For item effects, next_phase1, next_group is the selected group and next_index is path_index+1.
All reserved response words are zero.

statuses.0: Success: write exactly the first64 output bytes, preserve any tail, source and workspace.
statuses.4294967294: SHORT: request shorter than64 or output capacity below64. No writes. This check has highest priority.
statuses.4294967295: INVALID: request length differs from64, workspace length differs from0, unsupported revision/phase/group, nonzero reserved word or invalid continuation index. No writes.

continuation_scope: Caller-owned structural state. It does not authenticate a history of prior writer calls. The production adapter binds counts to immutable live affected vectors and returns after the first real writer error.
writer_contract: Keep each original writeln! invocation and literal format string; do not coalesce outputs or render all paths into one temporary string.
Preserve custom Write::write_fmt overrides, the default write_all partial-write and Interrupted handling, native PathBuf::display behavior, duplicates and embedded path bytes.
A writer error preserves already written bytes and stops all later writer operations.
Summary errors do not change the filesystem delta already committed by the public caller.
